title: Stem-changing verbs
topic: e → ie, o → ue, e → i, u → ue in the present tense
why: After querer and poder, this lesson extends the “boot” pattern to all the common stem-changing verbs: e → ie, o → ue, e → i and jugar. It's the last big group of present-tense irregulars before the unit review, practiced through likes, sports and eating out.

The boot: e → ie, o → ue

You already know quiero and puedo. Lots of very common verbs work the same way: the stressed vowel of the stem changes (it becomes a “diphthong”), but not with nosotros and vosotros, where the stress falls on the ending. Draw a line around the forms that change in the table and you get the shape of a boot, which is why these are often called “boot verbs.”

pensar (e → ie)preferir (e → ie)dormir (o → ue)volver (o → ue)
yopiensoprefieroduermovuelvo
túpiensasprefieresduermesvuelves
él, ella, ustedpiensaprefiereduermevuelve
nosotros, nosotraspensamospreferimosdormimosvolvemos
vosotros, vosotraspensáispreferísdormísvolvéis
ellos, ellas, ustedespiensanprefierenduermenvuelven

The endings, on the other hand, are perfectly regular: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an for -ar verbs, and so on. Only the stem moves.

Verbs to know

  • e → ie: pensar, empezar, preferir, cerrar, querer
  • o → ue: dormir, volver, poder, encontrar, costar

English has nothing like this in the present tense: “I think, we think” never changes. The closest thing is the vowel shift in pairs like “sing / sang” or “foot / feet.” In Spanish, just remember the boot: the vowel changes everywhere except we and you all.

Nosotros volvemos a las seis, pero Marta vuelve a las ocho.We get back at six, but Marta gets back at eight.

e → i and u → ue

A few -ir verbs change their e to i (not ie). They follow the same boot: nosotros and vosotros keep the e.

pedir (e → i)seguir (e → i)jugar (u → ue)
yopidosigojuego
túpidessiguesjuegas
él, ella, ustedpidesiguejuega
nosotros, nosotraspedimosseguimosjugamos
vosotros, vosotraspedísseguísjugáis
ellos, ellas, ustedespidensiguenjuegan

What to notice

  • e → i: pedir (to ask for, to order), repetir (to repeat), servir (to serve), seguir (to follow, to keep on).
  • Seguir drops its u in the first person: sigo. Before o, the hard “g” sound (as in “go”) is written with a plain g (as in tengo). Everywhere else you keep gu: sigues, sigue, siguen.
  • Jugar is the only u → ue verb: juego, juegas… Where English just says “play soccer,” Spanish needs a before the sport: jugar al fútbol, jugar al tenis (a + el = al).

Pedir or preguntar?

English uses “ask” for both, and only the little word “for” tells them apart. Spanish has two separate verbs:

VerbMeaningExample
pedirto ask for something, to orderPido un café. / Pido ayuda.
preguntarto ask a questionPregunto la hora. / Pregunto dónde está el baño.

In a restaurant, “I'll have a salad” is usually pido una ensalada (I'm ordering a salad). If there's a “for” after “ask” in your English, or you could add one, it's the first verb.

", "

Every day: likes, sports, eating out

These verbs come up all day long. Here are some sentences to learn as they are:

SpanishEnglish
Empiezo a trabajar a las nueve.I start work at nine.
Vuelvo a casa a las siete.I get home at seven.
Duermo ocho horas.I sleep eight hours.
Prefiero el té.I prefer tea.
¿Qué piensas?What do you think?
La tienda cierra a las nueve.The store closes at nine.
No encuentro las llaves.I can't find the keys.
¿Cuánto cuesta? ¿Cuánto cuestan?How much is it? How much are they?
El camarero sirve el vino.The waiter serves the wine.
Juego al pádel los martes.I play padel on Tuesdays.

You'll recognize ¿Cuánto cuesta?, which you learned as a set phrase: it's simply costar (o → ue) in the third person.

Empezar takes a before an infinitive: empiezo a trabajar, “I start to work.” English can say “start working” or “start to work”; Spanish only allows the second pattern, with the little word in between.

How do you know if a verb changes its stem? Dictionaries often show it in parentheses: pensar (ie), dormir (ue), pedir (i). Learn each new verb with its marker.

¿Qué prefieres, carne o pescado? Prefiero pescado.Which do you prefer, meat or fish? I prefer fish.
